title: Electrons, muons and the Reeb decomposition
html:
Remark. Electrons, muons and the Reeb decomposition

The Reeb decomposition (Reeb decomposition) applied to a Descartes universe yields two classes of fermionic excitations (fermion). The degree of the vertical component \alpha_V distinguishes them. Forms with \deg\alpha_V = 1 correspond to electrons, while forms with \deg\alpha_V = 2 correspond to muons. More generally, each additional unit of vertical degree identifies a successive lepton generation. The constraint \chi(\mathcal{S}) = -6 bounds the number of such generations, since the Hodge decomposition of \mathcal{S} admits only finitely many independent vertical harmonic forms. This generation-dependent structure produces testable predictions, including a q-correction to the proton charge radius that differs between muonic and electronic hydrogen (Section).
